scope: Owner and operator client layer for VowVault: permission-set construction, encrypted owner backup, mandate calldata, operator authorization and reservation reads
negativeChecks: A salt reused between two real leaves or between a real and a padding leaf is rejected before a root exists.
A permission naming a supplier claim key that is not a curve point is refused before it can occupy a committed slot.
A proof issued for one slot proves neither another slot, another leaf nor a changed root.
A requested amount above the committed cap, outside the approval window or past the request deadline never reaches a signature.
An operator signature does not verify after any change to mandate, root, permission, leaf hash, amount, request id or deadline, and a second operator key cannot authorize the same request.
A padding slot and an out-of-range slot cannot be turned into a reserve request.
A mandate whose root, token, owner, operator key, expiry or id differs from the local set is refused before funding.
Wrong chain, missing mandate, unreconcilable accounting and foreign reservation rows are refused instead of decoded.
A PurchaseReserved or ReservationClaimed event from another contract, reservation or amount is not accepted as this request's settlement.
limitations: TypeScript client tests only, against synthetic RPC responses and receipts; no VowVault has been declared, deployed, funded, reserved or claimed on any network.

The permission root, leaf, slot-0 proof and reservation-id domain encoding are asserted as identical constants in both languages; the reservation id is not asserted against the value an executed reserve() returned.
Calldata field order is verified against the local Cairo struct definitions, not against a chain-accepted transaction.
The mandate id must be predicted before create_mandate; the vault exposes no next-mandate view, so the client can only verify it after creation and before funding.
Random salts come from the platform crypto source and are checked for range, distinctness and independence across sets, not for generator quality.
Encryption at rest does not protect a compromised active browser or process; JavaScript strings holding a decrypted set cannot be zeroed.
